+### Plugin repositories
+
+HCLI ships with two built-in repositories (`hexrays` and `community`) that provide the public plugin index. You can add your own named repositories that point to a JSON index file, a local directory of plugin archives, or a [plugin bundle](../reference/plugin-bundle-spec.md) zip.
+
+```
+❯ hcli plugin repo list
+❯ hcli plugin repo add <name> <url>
+❯ hcli plugin repo remove <name>
+❯ hcli plugin repo set-default <name>
+```
+
+Repository URLs use the `https://` scheme for remote JSON indexes or `file://` for local paths. HCLI infers the repository type from what the path points to: a directory becomes a filesystem repository, a zip file containing `plugin-bundle.json` becomes a bundle repository, and anything else is treated as a JSON index.
+
+You can scope plugin references to a specific repository with a `repo/` prefix (e.g., `hcli plugin install myrepo/plugin-name`). Unprefixed references resolve against the default repository.
+
+### Offline and air-gapped environments
+
+Environments without internet access (for example, a FLARE-VM instance with host-only networking) can use a plugin bundle as their sole repository. A plugin bundle is a self-contained zip archive with plugins and their Python dependencies for specific platforms. See [Plugin Bundles](../reference/plugin-bundle-spec.md) for the format.
+
+To set this up, remove the default repositories (which require network access), add the bundle as a named repository, and set it as the default:
+
+```console
+❯ hcli plugin repo remove hexrays
+removed plugin repository 'hexrays'
+
+❯ hcli plugin repo remove community
+removed plugin repository 'community'
+
+❯ hcli plugin repo add offline file:///path/to/plugin-bundle.zip
+added plugin repository 'offline' -> file:///path/to/plugin-bundle.zip
+
+❯ hcli plugin repo set-default offline
+default plugin repository is now 'offline'
+
+❯ hcli plugin search
+current platform: windows-x86_64
+current version: 9.4
+
+ plugin1  1.0.0  ...
+
+❯ hcli plugin install plugin1
+Installed plugin: plugin1==1.0.0
+```
+
+Dependencies are installed from the bundle's embedded wheelhouse, so pip does not need network access.
+
+To restore the default configuration later, re-add the built-in repositories with their canonical URLs:
+
+```console
+❯ hcli plugin repo add hexrays https://hexrays.plugins.hex-rays.com/plugin-repository.json
+❯ hcli plugin repo add community https://community.plugins.hex-rays.com/plugin-repository.json
+```

2	
3	The IDA Plugin Manager can help you discover, install, and manage IDA plugins distributed via a central index. It simplifies extending IDA capabilities, whether the plugins are written in IDAPython or compiled languages like C/C++.

51	## Python environment
52	
53	Plugins that declare Python dependencies need a working Python environment. HCLI checks this before installing dependencies. If something is wrong, the install stops and points you to `hcli ida python doctor` for details. See [IDA's Python Environment](ida-python-environment.md) for setup.
54	
55	If your Python setup works but does not match the recommended configuration, pass `--no-python-environment-check` to skip the check:
56	
57	```console
58	❯ hcli plugin --no-python-environment-check install <name>
59	```
60	
61	## As a user of IDA...
62	
63	You'll want to know the HCLI commands:
64	
65	```
66	❯ hcli plugin search 
67	❯ hcli plugin search [keyword or plugin-name]
68	❯ hcli plugin install <plugin-name>
69	❯ hcli plugin status
70	❯ hcli plugin upgrade <plugin-name>
71	❯ hcli plugin uninstall <plugin-name>
72	```
73	
74	For offline or air-gapped environments, plugins can be installed from a plugin bundle archive. See [Plugin Bundles](../reference/plugin-bundle-spec.md) for details.
75	
76	Plugins are written to `$IDAUSR/plugins`, which is typically `~/.idapro/plugins` on Unix-like systems, where IDA Pro will load them the next time the application is opened.
77	
78	You can discover interesting plugins via:
79	
80	  - `hcli plugin search` CLI program, or
81	  - [plugins.hex-rays.com](https://plugins.hex-rays.com) website, or
82	  - [github.com/HexRaysSA/plugin-repository](https://github.com/HexRaysSA/plugin-repository) raw index data.
83	
84	HCLI supports installing plugins to be loaded by IDA 9.0 and newer.
85	
86	### Disambiguating plugin names
87	
88	When two plugins share the same bare name in the repository (for example, different forks of the same project), HCLI cannot tell which one you mean from the name alone. The `search`, `install`, and `upgrade` commands will print the ambiguous candidates and ask you to qualify the reference with the plugin's repository URL:
89	
90	```console
91	❯ hcli plugin install ida-chat
92	Error: plugin name 'ida-chat' is ambiguous
93	Choose one of:
94	  ida-chat@https://github.com/HexRaysSA/ida-chat-plugin
95	  ida-chat@https://github.com/tanu360/ida-chat-plugin
96	```
97	
98	You can pin the reference with `name@repository-url`, and optionally include a version spec:
99	
100	```console
101	❯ hcli plugin install ida-chat@https://github.com/HexRaysSA/ida-chat-plugin
102	❯ hcli plugin install ida-chat==1.0.0@https://github.com/HexRaysSA/ida-chat-plugin
103	```
104	
105	Because plugins install into `$IDAUSR/plugins/<name>`, only one plugin with a given bare name can be installed at a time. If you need to switch to a different same-named plugin from another repository, uninstall the current one first. Similarly, `upgrade` will not change the source repository: once a plugin is installed, its repository is recorded in the local metadata and upgrades are anchored to it.

40	def is_plugin_repo_host(url: str) -> bool:
41	    """Whether hcli credentials may be attached to a request for this URL.
42	
43	    True only for HTTPS on PLUGIN_REPO_HOST or a subdomain of it. The leading
44	    dot in the suffix test is what keeps "evilplugins.hex-rays.com" and
45	    "plugins.hex-rays.com.attacker.tld" out. Never plaintext HTTP, so a
46	    downgrade cannot carry a credential.
47	    """
48	    parsed = urlparse(url)
49	    if parsed.scheme != "https":
50	        return False
51	    host = (parsed.hostname or "").lower()
52	    return host == PLUGIN_REPO_HOST or host.endswith("." + PLUGIN_REPO_HOST)

55	def fetch_plugin_repo_bytes(url: str, repo_name: str | None = None) -> bytes:
56	    """Fetch plugin repository content: an index document or a plugin archive.
57	
58	    Accepts http and https, because fetch_plugin_archive routes both here; only
59	    https can ever carry credentials, and an https request that redirects to
60	    http is refused rather than downgraded.
61	
62	    Credentials are attached only on hops that land on a Hex-Rays plugin
63	    repository host, where they unlock entitled private plugins -- never to
64	    third parties (GitHub release assets, mirrors, presigned S3 URLs). Because
65	    httpx only strips Authorization across origins and would happily forward an
66	    x-api-key, redirects are walked by hand so the decision is remade per hop.
67	    """
68	    scheme = urlparse(url).scheme
69	
70	    # Resolved lazily on the first credential-eligible hop and reused: deciding
71	    # whether we are logged in can cost a network round-trip for interactive
72	    # credentials, so it must not repeat per redirect. Per hop we only decide
73	    # whether to attach what was already resolved.
74	    auth_headers: dict[str, str] | None = None
75	
76	    with httpx.Client(timeout=30.0, follow_redirects=False) as client:
77	        current_url = url
78	        # +1 because the initial request consumes an iteration; MAX_REDIRECTS
79	        # counts redirects actually followed.
80	        for _ in range(MAX_REDIRECTS + 1):
81	            credentialed = is_plugin_repo_host(current_url)
82	            if credentialed and auth_headers is None:
83	                # Deferred import: the auth service is only needed for our own hosts.
84	                from hcli.lib.auth import get_optional_auth_headers
85	
86	                auth_headers = get_optional_auth_headers()
87	
88	            headers = {"User-Agent": USER_AGENT}
89	            if credentialed and auth_headers:
90	                headers.update(auth_headers)
91	
92	            response = client.get(current_url, headers=headers)
93	
94	            # has_redirect_location, not is_redirect: is_redirect matches any
95	            # 3xx, but only those carrying a Location are followable. A 300 or
96	            # 304 falls through to raise_for_status, which names the real
97	            # status instead of a misleading missing-Location error.
98	            if response.has_redirect_location:
99	                next_url = str(httpx.URL(current_url).join(response.headers["location"]))
100	                if scheme == "https" and urlparse(next_url).scheme != "https":
101	                    raise ValueError(f"HTTPS request was redirected to insecure HTTP URL: {next_url}")
102	                current_url = next_url
103	                continue
104	
105	            # Only denials by our own hosts are entitlement-shaped, and only
106	            # 401/403: these hosts answer 401 for anything they will not serve,
107	            # so a 404 means the resource genuinely is not there and keeps its
108	            # own error. Mapping 404 to "log in" would tell a user to
109	            # authenticate against `community`, which needs no credentials.
110	            if credentialed:
111	                authenticated = bool(auth_headers)
112	                if response.status_code in (401, 403):
113	                    raise PluginAccessDeniedError(
114	                        url, response.status_code, authenticated=authenticated, repo_name=repo_name
115	                    )
116	
117	            response.raise_for_status()
118	            return response.content
119	
120	    raise ValueError(f"too many redirects while fetching: {url}")
121

123	def fetch_plugin_archive(url: str) -> bytes:
124	    parsed_url = urlparse(url)
125	
126	    if parsed_url.scheme == "file":
127	        file_path = Path(urllib.request.url2pathname(parsed_url.path))
128	        if not file_path.exists():
129	            raise FileNotFoundError(f"File not found: {file_path}")
130	        return file_path.read_bytes()
131	
132	    elif parsed_url.scheme in ("http", "https"):
133	        return fetch_plugin_repo_bytes(url)
134	
135	    else:
136	        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported URL scheme: {parsed_url.scheme}")

196	def get_plugin_by_name(plugins: list[Plugin], name: str, host: str | None = None) -> Plugin:
197	    """Find a plugin by name and, optionally, host.
198	
199	    Name matching is case-insensitive. Host matching, when supplied, uses
200	    normalized URL comparison so trailing-slash and casing differences do
201	    not prevent a match.
202	
203	    Raises:
204	        KeyError: when no matching plugin exists.
205	        AmbiguousPluginReferenceError: when the bare name matches multiple
206	            plugins and no host was provided to disambiguate.
207	    """
208	    wanted_name = name.lower()
209	    if host:
210	        normalized_host = normalize_plugin_host(host)
211	        matches = [
212	            plugin
213	            for plugin in plugins
214	            if plugin.name.lower() == wanted_name and normalize_plugin_host(plugin.host) == normalized_host
215	        ]
216	    else:
217	        matches = [plugin for plugin in plugins if plugin.name.lower() == wanted_name]
218	
219	    if not matches:
220	        raise KeyError(f"plugin not found: {name}")
221	
222	    if len(matches) > 1:
223	        logger.debug("ambiguous plugin reference, found matches:")
224	        for plugin in matches:
225	            logger.debug("  - %s (%s)", plugin.name, plugin.host)
226	
227	        candidates = [(plugin.name, plugin.host) for plugin in matches]
228	        raise AmbiguousPluginReferenceError(name, candidates)
229	
230	    return matches[0]

357	class PluginArchiveIndex:
358	    """index a collection of plugin archive URLs by name/version/idaVersion/platform.
359	
360	    Plugins are uniquely identified by the name and host (repo URL today, xor other canonical URL in the future).
361	    There may be multiple versions of a plugin.
362	    Each version may have multiple distribution archives due to:
363	      - different IDA versions (compiled against SDK for 7.4 versus 9.2)
364	      - different platforms (compiled for Windows, macOS, Linux)
365	    """
366	
367	    def __init__(self):
368	        # tuple[name, host] -> version -> tuple[set[IdaVersion], set[Platform]] -> list[tuple[url, sha256, metadata]]
369	        self.index: dict[
370	            tuple[str, str],
371	            dict[
372	                str,
373	                dict[tuple[frozenset[IdaVersion], frozenset[Platform]], list[tuple[str, str, IDAMetadataDescriptor]]],
374	            ],
375	        ] = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(list)))
376	
377	    def index_plugin_archive(
378	        self, buf: bytes, url: str, expected_host: str | None = None, context: dict[str, str] | None = None
379	    ):
380	        """Parse the given plugin archive and index the encountered plugins.
381	
382	        Optionally filter out plugins whose host does not match the expected host.
383	        """
384	        if context is None:
385	            context = {}
386	        logging.debug(m("indexing plugin archive: %s", url, **context))
387	        for path, metadata in get_metadatas_with_paths_from_plugin_archive(buf, context=context):
388	            try:
389	                validate_metadata_in_plugin_archive(buf, path, metadata)
390	            except ValueError as e:
391	                logger.debug(
392	                    m(
393	                        "failed to validate plugin metadata: %s",
394	                        path,
395	                        **dict(
396	                            context,
397	                            path=str(path),
398	                            plugin_name=metadata.plugin.name,
399	                            plugin_version=metadata.plugin.version,
400	                            error=str(e),
401	                        ),
402	                    )
403	                )
404	                return
405	
406	            h = hashlib.sha256()
407	            h.update(buf)
408	            sha256 = h.hexdigest()
409	
410	            name = metadata.plugin.name
411	            host = metadata.plugin.host
412	            normalized_host = normalize_plugin_host(host)
413	            version = metadata.plugin.version
414	            ida_versions = frozenset(metadata.plugin.ida_versions)
415	            platforms = frozenset(metadata.plugin.platforms)
416	            spec = (ida_versions, platforms)
417	
418	            if expected_host and normalize_plugin_host(expected_host) != normalized_host:
419	                logger.debug(m("host mismatch: %s: %s versus expected %s", name, host, expected_host, **context))
420	                continue
421	
422	            logger.debug(
423	                m(
424	                    "found valid plugin: %s",
425	                    path,
426	                    **dict(
427	                        context,
428	                        path=str(path),
429	                        plugin_name=metadata.plugin.name,
430	                        plugin_version=metadata.plugin.version,
431	                    ),
432	                )
433	            )
434	
435	            versions = self.index[(name.lower(), normalized_host)]
436	            specs = versions[version]
437	            specs[spec].append((url, sha256, metadata))
438	
439	    def get_plugins(self) -> list[Plugin]:
440	        """
441	        Fetch all plugins and their locations, indexed by name/version/ida version/platforms.
442	        The results are stably sorted.
443	        """
444	        ret = []
445	
446	        # sort alphabetically by name
447	        for id_, versions in sorted(self.index.items(), key=lambda p: p[0]):
448	            display_name, display_host = id_
449	            locations_by_version = defaultdict(list)
450	
451	            # sort by version
452	            for version, specs in sorted(versions.items(), key=lambda p: parse_plugin_version(p[0])):
453	                # sorted arbitrarily (but stably)
454	                for spec, urls in sorted(specs.items()):
455	                    # sorted arbitrarily (but stably)
456	                    for url, sha256, metadata in sorted(urls):
457	                        location = PluginArchiveLocation(
458	                            url=url,
459	                            sha256=sha256,
460	                            metadata=metadata,
461	                        )
462	                        locations_by_version[version].append(location)
463	                        display_name = metadata.plugin.name
464	
465	            plugin = Plugin(name=display_name, host=display_host, versions=locations_by_version)
466	            ret.append(plugin)
467	
468	        return ret

27	        return f"{name}: {'credentials rejected' if error.status_code == 401 else 'not entitled'}"
28	    if isinstance(error, (httpx.ConnectError, httpx.TimeoutException)):
29	        return f"{name}: unreachable"

39	class AggregatePluginRepo(BasePluginRepo):
40	    """Several named repositories presented as one.
41	
42	    Callers pass the scope they want -- one repository, or all of them. This
43	    class holds no notion of a default: which repository resolves an unprefixed
44	    reference is a configuration question, answered by the caller.
45	    """
46	
47	    def __init__(self, repositories: dict[str, PluginRepository]):
48	        super().__init__()
49	        self.repositories = repositories
50	        self._plugins: dict[str, list[Plugin]] = {}
51	        self._failures: dict[str, Exception] = {}
52	        self._dropped: dict[str, int] = {}
53	        # Which repository served which plugin, remembered at load time rather
54	        # than reconstructed later by scanning every loaded list.
55	        self._owner: dict[int, str] = {}
56	
57	    def _load(self, name: str) -> list[Plugin]:
58	        """Fetch one repository, at most once, remembering failure as well as success."""
59	        if name in self._plugins:
60	            return self._plugins[name]
61	        if name in self._failures:
62	            raise self._failures[name]
63	
64	        repo = self.repositories[name]
65	        try:
66	            plugins = JSONFilePluginRepo.from_url(repo.url, repo_name=name).get_plugins()
67	        except Exception as e:
68	            logger.debug("failed to fetch plugin repository %s (%s): %s", name, repo.url, e)
69	            self._failures[name] = e
70	            raise
71	
72	        kept = self._filter_entitled(name, plugins)
73	        self._plugins[name] = kept
74	        for plugin in kept:
75	            self._owner[id(plugin)] = name
76	        return kept
77	
78	    def _filter_entitled(self, name: str, plugins: list[Plugin]) -> list[Plugin]:
79	        """Drop plugins claiming an identity this repository may not assert.
80	
81	        Recorded rather than printed: a repository that could not fully answer
82	        is reported through notes(), the same way an unreachable one is, so
83	        --json callers see it too instead of only text-mode users.
84	        """
85	        if name == HEXRAYS_REPO_NAME:
86	            return plugins
87	
88	        kept = [p for p in plugins if _identity_host(p) != PLUGIN_REPO_HOST]
89	        dropped = len(plugins) - len(kept)
90	        if dropped:
91	            logger.debug("repository %s served %d plugin(s) claiming Hex-Rays identities", name, dropped)
92	            self._dropped[name] = dropped
93	        return kept
94	
95	    def notes(self) -> list[str]:
96	        """What the caller should know about repositories consulted so far.
97	
98	        Covers both a repository that could not be reached and one that was
99	        reached but served plugins it is not entitled to. Both mean the answer
100	        is not the whole picture, so both belong in the same report.
101	        """
102	        notes = []
103	        for name in self.repositories:
104	            if name in self._failures:
105	                notes.append(f"skipped -- {_describe_failure(name, self._failures[name])}")
106	            if name in self._dropped:
107	                notes.append(f"{name}: ignored {self._dropped[name]} plugin(s) claiming Hex-Rays identities")
108	        return notes
109	
110	    def get_plugins_in(self, name: str) -> list[Plugin]:
111	        """Plugins from one named repository. Propagates that repository's failure."""
112	        if name not in self.repositories:
113	            raise KeyError(f"unknown plugin repository: {name}")
114	        return list(self._load(name))
115	
116	    def get_plugins(self) -> list[Plugin]:
117	        """Every plugin hcli can see, across every configured repository.
118	
119	        Best-effort by design: one unreachable or unauthorized repository must
120	        not hide the results of the others, so failures are recorded and
121	        reported through notes() rather than raised.
122	        """
123	        plugins: list[Plugin] = []
124	        for name in self.repositories:
125	            try:
126	                plugins.extend(self._load(name))
127	            except Exception as e:
128	                logger.debug("skipping plugin repository %s: %s", name, e)
129	        return plugins
130	
131	    def repo_of(self, plugin: Plugin) -> str | None:
132	        """Which loaded repository served this plugin."""
133	        return self._owner.get(id(plugin))

32	def read_repos_file(path: Path) -> list[str]:
33	    if not path.exists():
34	        raise ValueError(f"file doesn't exist: {path}")
35	
36	    repos = []
37	    for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
38	        if not line:
39	            continue
40	        if line.startswith("#"):
41	            continue
42	
43	        repos.append(line.strip())
44	
45	    return repos

180	def repo_for_reference(ctx: click.Context, ref: PluginReference) -> hcli.lib.ida.plugin.repo.BasePluginRepo:
181	    """The repository a reference should be resolved against.
182	
183	    Unprefixed references resolve in the default repository; a "repo/" prefix
184	    resolves in that repository alone. Under an explicit --repo there is only
185	    one repository to search, so a prefix has nothing to select and is refused
186	    rather than silently ignored.
187	    """
188	    aggregate: AggregatePluginRepo | None = ctx.obj.get("plugin_repos")
189	
190	    if aggregate is None:
191	        if ref.repo:
192	            console.print(
193	                f"[red]Cannot use the repository prefix '{ref.repo}/' with --repo[/red]: "
194	                f"--repo already selects the only repository searched."
195	            )
196	            raise click.Abort()
197	        return ctx.obj["plugin_repo"]
198	
199	    name = ref.repo or ctx.obj["default_plugin_repo"]
200	    if name not in aggregate.repositories:
201	        if ref.repo:
202	            known = ", ".join(sorted(aggregate.repositories)) or "none"
203	            console.print(f"[red]Unknown plugin repository '{ref.repo}'[/red]. Configured: {known}")
204	        else:
205	            console.print(
206	                f"[red]The default plugin repository '{name}' is not configured[/red]. "
207	                f"Fix .Settings.default-plugin-repository in ida-config.json."
208	            )
209	        raise click.Abort()
210	
211	    # A named scope is a request for THAT repository: if it cannot be reached,
212	    # that is the answer, not a quietly smaller search.
213	    try:
214	        plugins = aggregate.get_plugins_in(name)
215	    except (httpx.ConnectError, httpx.TimeoutException):
216	        # The group callback used to catch this when it did the fetching. The
217	        # fetch moved here, and httpx connection errors often stringify to "",
218	        # so without this the user gets a bare "Error:".
219	        console.print(
220	            f"[red]Cannot connect to plugin repository '{name}' at "
221	            f"{aggregate.repositories[name].url} - network unavailable.[/red]"
222	        )
223	        console.print("Please check your internet connection.")
224	        raise click.Abort()
225	
226	    # The survey path reports these through the search result; on this path
227	    # there is no result to carry them, so say it here rather than drop a
228	    # plugin silently.
229	    for note in aggregate.notes():
230	        console.print(f"[yellow]Warning:[/yellow] repository {note}")
231	
232	    return hcli.lib.ida.plugin.repo.file.JSONFilePluginRepo(plugins)

87	def install_plugin(
88	    ctx, plugin: str, editable: bool, config: tuple[str, ...], no_build_isolation: bool, upgrade: bool
89	) -> None:
90	    """Install a plugin from a repository, local directory, local .zip file, or URL."""
91	    pip_options: PipOptions = ctx.obj.get("pip_options", PIP_OPTIONS_DEFAULT)
92	    if no_build_isolation:
93	        pip_options = dataclasses.replace(pip_options, no_build_isolation=True)
94	    check_environment = not ctx.obj.get("no_python_environment_check", False)
95	    plugin_repo_obj = ctx.obj.get("plugin_repo")
96	    plugin_spec = plugin
97	    try:
98	        sweep_trash()
99	
100	        with rich.status.Status("collecting environment", console=stderr_console):
101	            current_ida_platform = find_current_ida_platform()
102	            current_ida_version = find_current_ida_version()
103	
104	        # Editable install: skip the archive pipeline entirely. Read metadata
105	        # straight from the source directory and symlink it into place.
106	        if editable:
107	            source_dir = Path(plugin_spec).expanduser()
108	            if not source_dir.exists():
109	                raise click.BadParameter(f"path does not exist: {plugin_spec}")
110	            if not source_dir.is_dir():
111	                raise click.BadParameter(
112	                    f"--editable requires a directory containing ida-plugin.json, got: {plugin_spec}"
113	                )
114	            source_dir = source_dir.resolve()
115	            try:
116	                metadata = get_metadata_from_plugin_directory(source_dir)
117	            except ValueError as e:
118	                raise click.BadParameter(str(e))
119	            plugin_name = metadata.plugin.name
120	            buf = None  # sentinel: editable; no archive bytes
121	
122	        elif Path(plugin_spec).expanduser().is_dir() and (Path(plugin_spec).expanduser() / "ida-plugin.json").is_file():

124	            # zip and run it through the same archive pipeline used for zip /
125	            # URL / repo installs. The dir must contain ida-plugin.json -- any
126	            # bare directory name without metadata falls through so it can be
127	            # resolved as a repository plugin reference instead.
128	            logger.info("installing from the local file system (directory)")
129	            source_dir = Path(plugin_spec).expanduser().resolve()
130	            buf = pack_plugin_directory_to_zip(source_dir)
131	            items = list(get_metadatas_with_paths_from_plugin_archive(buf))
132	            if len(items) != 1:

135	
136	        elif Path(plugin_spec).exists() and plugin_spec.endswith(".zip"):

143	
144	        elif plugin_spec.startswith("file://"):
145	            logger.info("installing from the local file system")

149	            if len(items) != 1:

153	        elif is_github_direct_install_url(plugin_spec):

176	            except (httpx.ConnectError, httpx.TimeoutException):
177	                console.print(f"[red]Cannot connect to {plugin_spec} - network unavailable.[/red]")

286	                        console.print(f"Available targets in this bundle: {available}")
287	                        raise click.Abort()
288	                    effective_pip_options = merge_bundle_pip_options(pip_options, bundle_opts)
289	                    with rich.status.Status(status_text, console=stderr_console):
290	                        write_archive(
291	                            buf, plugin_name, pip_options=effective_pip_options, check_environment=check_environment
292	                        )
293	            else:
294	                with rich.status.Status(status_text, console=stderr_console):
295	                    write_archive(buf, plugin_name, pip_options=pip_options, check_environment=check_environment)
296	
297	        try:
298	            if metadata.plugin.settings:
299	                cli_config: dict[str, str | bool] = {}
300	                for config_item in config:
301	                    if "=" not in config_item:
302	                        raise ValueError(f"invalid config format: {config_item}, expected key=value")

304	                    descr = metadata.plugin.get_setting(key)

308	                if cli_config:

311	                        descr.validate_value(value)
312	                        if descr.default != value:

314	                else:
315	                    needed_settings = [
316	                        s
317	                        for s in metadata.plugin.settings
318	                        if not has_plugin_setting(plugin_name, s.key) and s.required and s.default is None
319	                    ]
320	
321	                    if needed_settings and not console.is_interactive:
322	                        setting_names = ", ".join(f"--config {s.key}=<value>" for s in needed_settings)
323	                        raise ValueError(
324	                            f"plugin requires configuration but console is not interactive. Please provide settings via command line: {setting_names}"
325	                        )
326	
327	                    if console.is_interactive:
328	                        existing_config = get_ida_config()
329	                        existing_values: dict[str, str | bool] = {}
330	                        if plugin_name in existing_config.plugins:
331	                            existing_values = dict(existing_config.plugins[plugin_name].settings)
332	
333	                        answers = prompt_plugin_settings(metadata.plugin.settings, existing_values)
334	                        if answers is None:
335	                            raise click.Abort()
336	                    else:
337	                        answers = {}
338	
339	                    for key, answer in answers.items():
340	                        descr = metadata.plugin.get_setting(key)
341	                        if descr.default == answer:
342	                            continue
343	
344	                        set_plugin_setting(metadata.plugin.name, descr.key, answer)
345	
346	        except Exception:
347	            if is_upgrade:

349	                # is now at the new version. Uninstalling it here would be a
350	                # worse outcome than leaving the settings unconfigured.
351	                logger.warning("failed to configure settings")

359	        verb = "Upgraded" if is_upgrade else "Installed"
360	        console.print(f"[green]{verb}[/green] plugin: [blue]{plugin_name}[/blue]=={metadata.plugin.version}{suffix}")
361	    except MissingCurrentInstallationDirectory:
362	        explain_missing_current_installation_directory(console)
363	        raise click.Abort()

23	from hcli.lib.ida.plugin.reference import normalize_plugin_host, parse_plugin_reference

31	@click.command()
32	@click.pass_context
33	@click.argument("plugin")
34	@click.option(
35	    "--no-build-isolation",
36	    is_flag=True,
37	    default=False,
38	    help="Disable pip build isolation when installing Python dependencies",
39	)
40	def upgrade_plugin(ctx, plugin: str, no_build_isolation: bool) -> None:
41	    """Upgrade an installed plugin to the latest compatible version."""
42	    pip_options: PipOptions = ctx.obj.get("pip_options", PIP_OPTIONS_DEFAULT)
43	    if no_build_isolation:
44	        pip_options = dataclasses.replace(pip_options, no_build_isolation=True)
45	    check_environment = not ctx.obj.get("no_python_environment_check", False)
46	    plugin_spec = plugin
47	    try:
48	        sweep_trash()
49	
50	        current_ida_platform = find_current_ida_platform()
51	        current_ida_version = find_current_ida_version()
52	
53	        if Path(plugin_spec).exists() and plugin_spec.endswith(".zip"):
54	            raise ValueError("cannot upgrade using local file; uninstall/reinstall instead")
55	
56	        if plugin_spec.startswith("file://"):
57	            raise ValueError("cannot upgrade using local file; uninstall/reinstall instead")
58	
59	        if plugin_spec.startswith("https://"):
60	            raise ValueError("cannot upgrade using URL; uninstall/reinstall instead")
61	
62	        try:
63	            ref = parse_plugin_reference(plugin_spec)
64	        except ValueError as e:
65	            raise click.BadParameter(f"invalid plugin reference: {plugin_spec!r}: {e}")
66	
67	        # Resolve the installed plugin first so we can anchor the upgrade to
68	        # the repository the user currently has installed. This avoids
69	        # switching repositories implicitly and also resolves the host for
70	        # bare-name upgrades even when the repository has a colliding name.
71	        try:
72	            installed = find_installed_plugin(ref.name)
73	        except PluginNotInstalledError:
74	            console.print(f"[red]Error[/red]: plugin '{ref.name}' is not installed")
75	            raise click.Abort()
76	
77	        if ref.host is not None and normalize_plugin_host(installed.host) != normalize_plugin_host(ref.host):
78	            console.print(
79	                f"[red]Error[/red]: installed plugin '{installed.name}' comes from {installed.host}, not {ref.host}"
80	            )
81	            console.print(
82	                "Upgrade cannot switch repositories. Uninstall first, then install the other qualified plugin."
83	            )
84	            raise click.Abort()
85	
86	        # Anchor the lookup to the installed host regardless of whether the
87	        # user supplied it. This is what makes bare-name upgrades work even
88	        # when the repository has a colliding name.
89	        bare_spec = ref.name + ref.version_spec
90	        logger.info("finding plugin in repository")
91	        # An upgrade is anchored to the installed name@host, so it may resolve
92	        # across every configured repository -- the plugin's identity, not the
93	        # default scope, decides which one answers. An explicit prefix narrows
94	        # that to one repository, mirroring the @host check above.
95	        if ref.repo:
96	            from hcli.commands.plugin import repo_for_reference
97	
98	            plugin_repo: BasePluginRepo = repo_for_reference(ctx, ref)
99	        else:
100	            plugin_repo = ctx.obj["plugin_repo"]
101	        try:
102	            plugin_name, buf = plugin_repo.fetch_compatible_plugin_from_spec(
103	                bare_spec, current_ida_platform, current_ida_version, host=installed.host
104	            )
105	        except (httpx.ConnectError, httpx.TimeoutException):
106	            console.print("[red]Cannot connect to plugin repository - network unavailable.[/red]")
107	            console.print("Please check your internet connection.")
108	            raise click.Abort()
109	
110	        if isinstance(plugin_repo, PluginBundleRepo) and not pip_options.has_custom_sources:
111	            from hcli.lib.ida.python import detect_current_python_version, merge_bundle_pip_options
112	
113	            current_python_version = detect_current_python_version()
114	            with bundle_dependency_source(plugin_repo, current_ida_platform, current_python_version) as bundle_opts:
115	                if bundle_opts is None:
116	                    available = ", ".join(plugin_repo.target_ids) or "none"
117	                    console.print(
118	                        f"[red]Error[/red]: plugin bundle does not include dependencies"
119	                        f" for {current_ida_platform}, Python {current_python_version}."
120	                    )
121	                    console.print(f"Available targets in this bundle: {available}")
122	                    raise click.Abort()
123	                effective_pip_options = merge_bundle_pip_options(pip_options, bundle_opts)
124	                upgrade_plugin_archive(
125	                    buf, plugin_name, pip_options=effective_pip_options, check_environment=check_environment
126	                )
127	        else:
128	            upgrade_plugin_archive(buf, plugin_name, pip_options=pip_options, check_environment=check_environment)
129	
130	        _, metadata = get_metadata_from_plugin_archive(buf, plugin_name)
131	
132	        console.print(f"[green]Installed[/green] plugin: [blue]{plugin_name}[/blue]=={metadata.plugin.version}")
133	    except MissingCurrentInstallationDirectory:
134	        explain_missing_current_installation_directory(console)
135	        raise click.Abort()
136	
137	    except FailedToDetectIDAVersion:
138	        explain_failed_to_detect_ida_version(console)
139	        raise click.Abort()
140	
141	    except KeyError as e:
142	        # get_plugins() drops repositories it could not consult, so a miss here
143	        # may mean "your session expired", not "no such plugin". Say which.
144	        logger.debug("error: %s", e, exc_info=True)
145	        console.print(f"[red]Error[/red]: {e}")
146	        aggregate = ctx.obj.get("plugin_repos")
147	        if aggregate is not None:
148	            for note in aggregate.notes():
149	                console.print(f"[yellow]Warning:[/yellow] repository {note}")
150	        raise click.Abort()
151	
152	    except click.Abort:
153	        raise
154	
155	    except Exception as e:
156	        logger.debug("error: %s", e, exc_info=True)
157	        console.print(f"[red]Error[/red]: {e}")
158	        raise click.Abort()

42	@dataclass

44	class IdaProduct:
45	    product: str
46	    major: int
47	    minor: int
48	    suffix: str | None = None
49	
50	    @classmethod
51	    def from_installer_filename(cls, filename: str):
52	        """Parse IDA installer filename to extract version information.
53	
54	        Args:
55	            filename: IDA installer filename (e.g., 'ida-pro_92_x64linux.run')
56	
57	        Raises:
58	            ValueError: If filename format is not recognized
59	        """
60	        basename = filename
61	        for ext in [".app.zip", ".run", ".exe"]:
62	            if basename.endswith(ext):
63	                basename = basename[: -len(ext)]
64	                break
65	
66	        # filename pattern: ida-{product}_{version}_{platform}
67	        match = re.match(r"^ida-([^_]+)_(\d{2})(sp\d+)?_", basename)
68	        if not match:
69	            raise ValueError(f"Unrecognized installer filename format: {filename}")
70	
71	        product_part = match.group(1)  # like: pro, home-pc, essential
72	        version_major = int(match.group(2)[0])  # like: 9
73	        version_minor = int(match.group(2)[1])  # like: 1
74	        suffix = match.group(3) or None  # like: sp1
75	
76	        product_mapping = {
77	            "pro": "IDA Professional",
78	            "classroom": "IDA Classroom",
79	            "essential": "IDA Essential",
80	            "free": "IDA Free",
81	            "home-arm": "IDA Home (ARM)",
82	            "home-mips": "IDA Home (MIPS)",
83	            "home-pc": "IDA Home (PC)",
84	            "home-ppc": "IDA Home (PPC)",
85	            "home-riscv": "IDA Home (RISC-V)",
86	            # Backwards-compatible aliases used by older portal assets.
87	            "classroom-free": "IDA Classroom",
88	            "free-pc": "IDA Free",
89	        }
90	
91	        product = product_mapping.get(product_part, f"IDA {product_part.title()}")
92	        return cls(product, version_major, version_minor, suffix)
93	
94	    def __str__(self):
95	        base = f"{self.product} {self.major}.{self.minor}"
96	        return f"{base}{self.suffix}" if self.suffix else base
97	
98	    def __lt__(self, other):
99	        if not isinstance(other, IdaProduct):
100	            return NotImplemented
101	        return (self.product, self.major, self.minor, self.suffix or "") < (
102	            other.product,
103	            other.major,
104	            other.minor,
105	            other.suffix or "",
106	        )

109	def get_ida_user_dir() -> Path:
110	    """Get the IDA Pro user directory."""

112	        return Path(ENV.HCLI_IDAUSR)
113	
114	    if ENV.IDAUSR is not None:
115	        return Path(ENV.IDAUSR.split(os.pathsep)[0])
116	
117	    os_ = get_os()
118	    if os_ == "windows":
119	        appdata = os.environ.get("APPDATA")
120	        if not appdata:
121	            raise ValueError("Failed to determine %APPDATA% location: environment variable not set")
122	
123	        return Path(appdata) / "Hex-Rays" / "IDA Pro"
124	    elif os_ in ("linux", "mac"):
125	        home = os.environ.get("HOME")
126	        if not home:
127	            raise ValueError("Failed to determine home directory: environment variable not set")
128	        return Path(home) / ".idapro"

151	def get_default_ida_install_directory(ver: IdaProduct) -> Path:
152	    """Get the default installation directory for IDA Pro."""
153	
154	    # like "IDA Professional 9.1sp1"
155	    app_directory_name = str(ver)
156	
157	    os_ = get_os()
158	    if os_ == "windows":
159	        return Path(os.environ.get("ProgramFiles", r"C:\Program Files")) / app_directory_name
160	    elif os_ == "linux":
161	        # workaround for #99: idat from IDA 9.2 on Linux fails to start if the path contains a space.
162	        # so we avoid using the path component "IDA Professional 9.2" and instead use "IDA-Professional-9.2"
163	        # which is ugly but works.
164	        #
165	        # idat is only used to discover the path to IDA's Python interpreter (when pip
166	        # dependencies need to be installed). Version and platform are detected statically.
167	        #
168	        # see also the warnings in commands/ida/install.py.
169	        #
170	        # this is confirmed to be fixed in IDA 9.3 for Linux
171	        if ver.major == 9 and ver.minor == 2 and " " in app_directory_name:
172	            # "IDA Professional 9.2" -> "IDA-Professional-9.2"
173	            sanitized_name = app_directory_name.replace(" ", "-")
174	            logger.info(

274	def _dedupe_paths(paths: list[Path]) -> list[Path]:
275	    """Deduplicate by resolved path, preserving first-seen order."""
276	    seen: set[Path] = set()
277	    ret: list[Path] = []
278	    for p in paths:
279	        try:
280	            key = p.resolve()
281	        except OSError:
282	            key = p
283	        if key in seen:
284	            continue
285	        seen.add(key)
286	        ret.append(p)

290	def _find_windows_registry_installations() -> list[_WindowsRegistryInstallation]:
291	    r"""Read IDA installation metadata from the Add/Remove Programs registry under HKLM.
292	
293	    The installer writes a key per install under
294	    ``HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\IDA <edition> <version>``.
295	    """
296	    try:
297	        import winreg as _winreg  # type: ignore[import-not-found]
298	    except ImportError:
299	        return []
300	
301	    winreg: Any = _winreg
302	    ret: list[_WindowsRegistryInstallation] = []
303	    uninstall_path = r"Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall"
304	    try:
305	        root = winreg.OpenKey(winreg.HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE, uninstall_path, 0, winreg.KEY_READ)
306	    except OSError:
307	        return ret
308	
309	    try:
310	        i = 0
311	        while True:
312	            try:
313	                subkey_name = winreg.EnumKey(root, i)
314	            except OSError:
315	                break
316	            i += 1
317	            try:
318	                with winreg.OpenKey(root, subkey_name, 0, winreg.KEY_READ) as subkey:
319	                    try:
320	                        display_name, _ = winreg.QueryValueEx(subkey, "DisplayName")
321	                    except OSError:
322	                        continue
323	                    if not isinstance(display_name, str) or not _is_ida_install_dir_name(display_name):
324	                        continue
325	                    try:
326	                        install_location, _ = winreg.QueryValueEx(subkey, "InstallLocation")
327	                    except OSError:
328	                        continue
329	                    if not install_location:
330	                        continue
331	                    display_version = None
332	                    try:
333	                        raw_display_version, _ = winreg.QueryValueEx(subkey, "DisplayVersion")
334	                    except OSError:
335	                        pass
336	                    else:
337	                        if isinstance(raw_display_version, str):
338	                            display_version = raw_display_version
339	                    path = Path(install_location)
340	                    if is_ida_dir(path):
341	                        ret.append(_WindowsRegistryInstallation(path, display_name, display_version))
342	            except OSError:
343	                continue
344	    finally:
345	        winreg.CloseKey(root)
346	    return ret
347

350	    """Read InstallLocation from the Add/Remove Programs registry under HKLM."""
351	    return [installation.path for installation in _find_windows_registry_installations()]

372	def _find_linux_installs_from_desktop_files() -> list[Path]:
373	    """Parse ``com.hex_rays.IDA.*.desktop`` shortcut files to recover install dirs.
374	
375	    The installer writes a desktop entry whose ``Exec=`` points at ``<installdir>/ida``,
376	    so the parent of that path is the install directory regardless of where the user
377	    chose to install.
378	    """
379	    ret: list[Path] = []
380	
381	    search_dirs: list[Path] = []
382	    xdg = os.environ.get("XDG_DATA_HOME")
383	    if xdg:
384	        search_dirs.append(Path(xdg) / "applications")
385	    search_dirs.extend((get_user_home_dir() / ".local" / "share" / "applications", Path("/usr/share/applications")))
386	
387	    for app_dir in search_dirs:
388	        if not app_dir.exists():
389	            continue
390	        for desktop in app_dir.glob("com.hex_rays.IDA.*.desktop"):
391	            try:
392	                text = desktop.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
393	            except OSError:
394	                continue
395	            for line in text.splitlines():
396	                if not line.startswith("Exec="):
397	                    continue
398	                # Exec= can include arguments; the binary is the first whitespace-separated token.
399	                exec_value = line[len("Exec=") :].strip()
400	                if not exec_value:
401	                    break
402	                exec_path = Path(exec_value.split()[0])
403	                install_dir = exec_path.parent
404	                if is_ida_dir(install_dir):
405	                    ret.append(install_dir)
406	                break
407	    return ret

565	def install_ida(installer: Path, install_dir: Path):
566	    r"""
567	    Install IDA Pro from an installer.
568	
569	    Args:
570	      installer: path to the installer downloaded from the Hex-Rays portal.
571	      install_dir: path to the installation directory, which should not already exist.
572	
573	    Installation directory should look like:
574	      - %Program Files%\IDA Professional 9.1\
575	      - /Applications/IDA Professional 9.1.app/
576	      - /opt/ida-9.1/
577	      - /tmp/ida-9.1/
578	      - ...
579	    """
580	    if install_dir.exists():
581	        raise FileExistsError(
582	            f"Installation directory already exists: {install_dir}\n"
583	            f"Please remove the existing directory first or choose a different location."
584	        )
585	
586	    logger.info(f"Installing IDA in {install_dir}")
587	
588	    installer_size = installer.stat().st_size
589	    check_free_space(install_dir.parent, installer_size * 3)
590	
591	    install_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
592	
593	    try:
594	        current_os = get_os()
595	        if current_os == "mac":
596	            _install_ida_mac(installer, install_dir)
597	        elif current_os == "linux":
598	            _install_ida_unix(installer, install_dir)
599	        elif current_os == "windows":
600	            _install_ida_windows(installer, install_dir)
601	        else:
602	            raise ValueError(f"unsupported OS: {current_os}")
603	    except Exception as e:
604	        logger.error(f"Installation failed: {e}")
605	        raise
606	
607	    contents = list(install_dir.iterdir())
608	    logger.debug("installed contents: %s", contents)
609	    if not len(contents):
610	        raise RuntimeError("installation failed: installation directory contents not created")
611	
612	    has_ida_hlp = False
613	    for _, _, files in os.walk(install_dir):
614	        if "ida.hlp" in files:
615	            has_ida_hlp = True
616	
617	    if not has_ida_hlp:
618	        raise RuntimeError("installation failed: ida.hlp not created")

621	def _install_ida_mac(installer: Path, prefix: Path) -> None:
622	    """Install IDA on macOS."""
623	    if not shutil.which("unzip"):
624	        raise RuntimeError("unzip is required to install IDA on macOS")
625	
626	    with (
627	        tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="hcli_") as temp_unpack_dir,
628	        tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="hcli_") as temp_install_dir,
629	    ):
630	        logger.info(f"Unpacking installer to {temp_unpack_dir}...")
631	
632	        # Unpack the installer
633	        process = subprocess.run(
634	            ["unzip", "-qq", str(installer), "-d", temp_unpack_dir], capture_output=True, check=False
635	        )
636	
637	        if process.returncode != 0:
638	            raise RuntimeError("Failed to unpack installer")
639	
640	        entries = list(Path(temp_unpack_dir).iterdir())
641	        if len(entries) != 1:
642	            raise ValueError(f"unexpected contents of zip archive: {len(entries)} root directories")
643	
644	        # typically this is the app name, like `ida-pro_90_armmac.app`
645	        # however the directory name might not be precisely the same as the zip archive filename
646	        # such as in SP releases.
647	        app_name = entries[0]
648	
649	        installer_path = None
650	        for platform in ("osx-arm64", "osx-x86_64"):
651	            candidate_path = Path(temp_unpack_dir) / app_name / "Contents" / "MacOS" / platform
652	            if candidate_path.exists():
653	                installer_path = candidate_path
654	                break
655	
656	        if not installer_path:
657	            raise RuntimeError("Installer executable not found")
658	
659	        logger.info(f"Running installer {app_name}...")
660	        temp_install_path = Path(temp_install_dir)
661	        args = _get_installer_args(temp_install_path)
662	
663	        process = subprocess.run([str(installer_path)] + args, capture_output=True, check=False)
664	
665	        if process.returncode != 0:
666	            raise RuntimeError("Installer execution failed")
667	
668	        # Find installed folder and copy to prefix
669	        installed_folders = list(temp_install_path.iterdir())
670	
671	        if not installed_folders:
672	            raise RuntimeError("No installation found after running installer")
673	
674	        install_folder = installed_folders[0]
675	        _copy_dir(install_folder, prefix)

726	def _copy_dir(src_path: Path, dest_path: Path) -> None:
727	    """Copy directory recursively."""
728	    if not src_path.exists():
729	        return
730	
731	    dest_path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
732	
733	    for item in src_path.rglob("*"):
734	        relative_path = item.relative_to(src_path)
735	        dest_item = dest_path / relative_path
736	
737	        if item.is_dir():

739	        elif item.is_file():
740	            dest_item.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
741	            try:
742	                shutil.copy2(item, dest_item)
743	            except OSError as e:
744	                if e.errno == errno.ENOSPC:
745	                    if dest_item.exists():

747	                    raise NoSpaceError(dest_path) from e

757	class PathsConfig(BaseModel):

761	    # Note: IDA itself may write the inner "Contents/MacOS" path here;
762	    # callers normalize via _normalize_install_dir().

773	# so a config file cannot repoint "hexrays" at a host of its own choosing and

881	def _migrate_plugin_repositories(config: IDAConfigJson) -> bool:
882	    """Bring a pre-0.23 single-repository config up to the named-repository map.
883	
884	    Returns True when the config was changed and should be written back.
885	
886	    One-shot by construction: the legacy ``plugin-repository`` key is removed by
887	    the rewrite, so this cannot re-trigger and needs no marker. A user who had
888	    customised that URL keeps it -- as a repository named "custom" that becomes
889	    the default -- because it is far more likely to be a repository of their own
890	    than a mirror of ours, and pointing the default at it is what preserves
891	    their unprefixed installs.
892	    """
893	    settings = config.settings
894	    if settings.plugin_repositories:
895	        return False
896	
897	    legacy = settings.plugin_repository
898	    if legacy is None:
899	        # Nothing to migrate: a fresh install with no config file, or a config
900	        # that never carried the setting. The reserved repositories are
901	        # synthesized on read, so there is no reason to create or rewrite the
902	        # file -- a read-only command must not announce a change it had no
903	        # cause to make.
904	        return False
905	
906	    legacy_url = legacy.url
907	    customised = bool(legacy_url) and legacy_url != LEGACY_PLUGIN_REPOSITORY_URL
908	
909	    repos = {name: PluginRepositoryConfig(url=url) for name, url in RESERVED_PLUGIN_REPOSITORIES.items()}
910	    default = COMMUNITY_REPO_NAME
911	
912	    if customised:
913	        name = "custom"
914	        suffix = 2
915	        while name in repos:
916	            name = f"custom-{suffix}"
917	            suffix += 1
918	        repos[name] = PluginRepositoryConfig(url=legacy_url)
919	        default = name
920	
921	    settings.plugin_repositories = repos
922	    settings.default_plugin_repository = default
923	    settings.plugin_repository = None
924	    return True
925

927	def get_plugin_repositories(config: IDAConfigJson | None = None) -> dict[str, PluginRepository]:
928	    """The configured plugin repositories, keyed by name.
929	
930	    Migrates a pre-0.23 config on first read. The two reserved repositories are
931	    always present with their shipped URLs: a file that tries to redefine them
932	    is ignored on that point and told so, since the whole value of a reserved
933	    name is that it cannot be pointed somewhere else.
934	    """
935	    if config is None:
936	        config = get_ida_config()
937	
938	    if _migrate_plugin_repositories(config):
939	        logger.info("migrating ida-config.json to named plugin repositories")
940	        try:
941	            set_ida_config(config)
942	        except OSError as e:
943	            # A read-only $IDAUSR must not break every plugin command; the new
944	            # layout still applies in memory for this process. Deliberately
945	            # quiet: the migration is retried on the next command, and
946	            # announcing a change that did not happen -- every time -- is worse
947	            # than saying nothing.
948	            logger.warning("could not persist plugin repository migration to %s: %s", get_ida_config_path(), e)
949	        else:
950	            stderr_console.print(
951	                f"[yellow]Note:[/yellow] {get_ida_config_path()} was updated to the new named plugin repository layout."
952	            )
953	
954	    repos: dict[str, PluginRepository] = {}
955	    for name, entry in config.settings.plugin_repositories.items():
956	        if name in RESERVED_PLUGIN_REPOSITORIES:
957	            continue
958	        if not PLUGIN_REPOSITORY_NAME_RE.match(name):
959	            # escape(): the pattern contains a character class, which Rich
960	            # would otherwise consume as markup and print as "^+$".
961	            stderr_console.print(
962	                f"[yellow]Warning:[/yellow] ignoring plugin repository {name!r}: "
963	                f"names must match {escape(PLUGIN_REPOSITORY_NAME_RE.pattern)}"
964	            )
965	            continue
966	        if not entry.url:
967	            stderr_console.print(f"[yellow]Warning:[/yellow] ignoring plugin repository {name!r}: no url")
968	            continue
969	        repos[name] = PluginRepository(name=name, url=entry.url, reserved=False)
970	
971	    for name, url in RESERVED_PLUGIN_REPOSITORIES.items():
972	        configured = config.settings.plugin_repositories.get(name)
973	        if configured is not None and configured.url and configured.url != url:
974	            stderr_console.print(
975	                f"[yellow]Warning:[/yellow] ignoring the url configured for reserved plugin repository "
976	                f"{name!r}; it always resolves to {url}"
977	            )
978	        repos[name] = PluginRepository(name=name, url=url, reserved=True)
979	
980	    return repos

1048

1312	def detect_binary_arch(path: Path) -> str | None:
1313	    """Detect the CPU architecture of a native binary by reading its header.
1314	
1315	    Supports PE (Windows), ELF (Linux), and Mach-O (macOS) formats.
1316	    Returns "x86_64" or "aarch64", or None if unrecognized.
1317	    """
1318	    with open(path, "rb") as f:
1319	        header = f.read(64)
1320	
1321	    if len(header) < 20:
1322	        return None
1323	
1324	    # ELF: magic = 0x7f 'E' 'L' 'F'
1325	    if header[:4] == b"\x7fELF":
1326	        e_machine = struct.unpack_from("<H", header, 18)[0]
1327	        return {0x3E: "x86_64", 0xB7: "aarch64"}.get(e_machine)
1328	
1329	    # PE: DOS MZ header
1330	    if header[:2] == b"MZ" and len(header) >= 0x40:
1331	        pe_offset = struct.unpack_from("<I", header, 0x3C)[0]
1332	        with open(path, "rb") as f:
1333	            f.seek(pe_offset)
1334	            pe_header = f.read(6)
1335	        if len(pe_header) >= 6 and pe_header[:4] == b"PE\0\0":
1336	            machine = struct.unpack_from("<H", pe_header, 4)[0]
1337	            return {0x8664: "x86_64", 0xAA64: "aarch64"}.get(machine)
1338	
1339	    # Mach-O 64-bit
1340	    magic = struct.unpack_from("<I", header, 0)[0]
1341	    if magic == 0xFEEDFACF:  # little-endian
1342	        cpu_type = struct.unpack_from("<I", header, 4)[0]
1343	        return {0x01000007: "x86_64", 0x0100000C: "aarch64"}.get(cpu_type)
1344	    elif magic == 0xCFFAEDFE:  # big-endian
1345	        cpu_type = struct.unpack_from(">I", header, 4)[0]
1346	        return {0x01000007: "x86_64", 0x0100000C: "aarch64"}.get(cpu_type)
1347	
1348	    return None

1468	    """Parse an IDA instance version for ordering.
1469	
1470	    Prefer Windows registry metadata when available, then the SDK version
1471	    embedded in python/ida_pro.py, then the main IDA executable. Fall back to
1472	    the installation path and configured instance name, so non-standard paths
1473	    still work when the user names the instance with a version.
1474	    """
1475	    version_sources: tuple[Callable[[], str | None], ...] = (
1476	        lambda: parse_version_from_windows_registry(ida_dir),
1477	        lambda: parse_version_from_ida_pro_py(ida_dir),
1478	        lambda: parse_version_from_ida_binary(get_ida_binary_path(ida_dir)),
1479	        lambda: parse_version_from_dir_name(ida_dir),
1480	        lambda: parse_version_from_dir_name(Path(name)),
1481	    )
1482	
1483	    for get_raw_version in version_sources:
1484	        raw_version = get_raw_version()
1485	        if raw_version is None:
1486	            continue
1487	        try:
1488	            return Version(raw_version)

2	
3	Repositories are fetched independently and merged here, in the client, so the
4	name a plugin was found under is always known -- unlike a server-side merge,
5	which would hand back one anonymous document.
6	"""

8	from __future__ import annotations
9	
10	import logging
11	from urllib.parse import urlparse
12	
13	import httpx
14	
15	from hcli.lib.ida import HEXRAYS_REPO_NAME, PluginRepository
16	from hcli.lib.ida.plugin.exceptions import PluginAccessDeniedError
17	from hcli.lib.ida.plugin.repo import PLUGIN_REPO_HOST, BasePluginRepo, Plugin, repo_from_url
18	
19	logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
20	
21	
22	def _describe_failure(name: str, error: Exception) -> str:
23	    if isinstance(error, PluginAccessDeniedError):
24	        if not error.authenticated:
25	            return f"{name}: not logged in"
26	        return f"{name}: {'credentials rejected' if error.status_code == 401 else 'not entitled'}"
27	    if isinstance(error, (httpx.ConnectError, httpx.TimeoutException)):
28	        return f"{name}: unreachable"
29	    if isinstance(error, httpx.HTTPStatusError):
30	        return f"{name}: HTTP {error.response.status_code}"
31	    return f"{name}: {error}"
32	
33	
34	def _identity_host(plugin: Plugin) -> str:
35	    return (urlparse(plugin.host).hostname or "").lower()
36	
37	
38	class AggregatePluginRepo(BasePluginRepo):
39	    """Several named repositories presented as one.
40	
41	    Callers pass the scope they want -- one repository, or all of them. This
42	    class holds no notion of a default: which repository resolves an unprefixed
43	    reference is a configuration question, answered by the caller.
44	    """
45	
46	    def __init__(self, repositories: dict[str, PluginRepository]):
47	        super().__init__()
48	        self.repositories = repositories
49	        self._plugins: dict[str, list[Plugin]] = {}
50	        self._repos: dict[str, BasePluginRepo] = {}
51	        self._failures: dict[str, Exception] = {}
52	        self._dropped: dict[str, int] = {}
53	        self._owner: dict[int, str] = {}
54	
55	    def _load(self, name: str) -> list[Plugin]:
56	        """Fetch one repository, at most once, remembering failure as well as success."""
57	        if name in self._plugins:
58	            return self._plugins[name]
59	        if name in self._failures:
60	            raise self._failures[name]
61	
62	        repo_config = self.repositories[name]
63	        try:
64	            child = repo_from_url(repo_config.url, repo_name=name)
65	            plugins = child.get_plugins()
66	        except Exception as e:
67	            logger.debug("failed to fetch plugin repository %s (%s): %s", name, repo_config.url, e)
68	            self._failures[name] = e
69	            raise
70	
71	        self._repos[name] = child
72	        kept = self._filter_entitled(name, plugins)
73	        self._plugins[name] = kept
74	        for plugin in kept:
75	            self._owner[id(plugin)] = name
76	        return kept
77	
78	    def _filter_entitled(self, name: str, plugins: list[Plugin]) -> list[Plugin]:
79	        """Drop plugins claiming an identity this repository may not assert.
80	
81	        Recorded rather than printed: a repository that could not fully answer
82	        is reported through notes(), the same way an unreachable one is, so
83	        --json callers see it too instead of only text-mode users.
84	        """
85	        if name == HEXRAYS_REPO_NAME:
86	            return plugins
87	
88	        kept = [p for p in plugins if _identity_host(p) != PLUGIN_REPO_HOST]
89	        dropped = len(plugins) - len(kept)
90	        if dropped:
91	            logger.debug("repository %s served %d plugin(s) claiming Hex-Rays identities", name, dropped)
92	            self._dropped[name] = dropped
93	        return kept
94	
95	    def notes(self) -> list[str]:
96	        """What the caller should know about repositories consulted so far.
97	
98	        Covers both a repository that could not be reached and one that was
99	        reached but served plugins it is not entitled to. Both mean the answer
100	        is not the whole picture, so both belong in the same report.
101	        """
102	        notes = []
103	        for name in self.repositories:
104	            if name in self._failures:
105	                notes.append(f"skipped -- {_describe_failure(name, self._failures[name])}")
106	            if name in self._dropped:
107	                notes.append(f"{name}: ignored {self._dropped[name]} plugin(s) claiming Hex-Rays identities")
108	        return notes
109	
110	    def get_child_repo(self, name: str) -> BasePluginRepo:
111	        """The loaded repo object for a named repository.
112	
113	        Triggers loading if not already loaded. Propagates that repository's failure.
114	        """
115	        if name not in self.repositories:
116	            raise KeyError(f"unknown plugin repository: {name}")
117	        self._load(name)
118	        return self._repos[name]
119	
120	    def get_plugins_in(self, name: str) -> list[Plugin]:
121	        """Plugins from one named repository. Propagates that repository's failure."""
122	        if name not in self.repositories:
123	            raise KeyError(f"unknown plugin repository: {name}")
124	        return list(self._load(name))
125	
126	    def get_plugins(self) -> list[Plugin]:
127	        """Every plugin hcli can see, across every configured repository.
128	
129	        Best-effort by design: one unreachable or unauthorized repository must
130	        not hide the results of the others, so failures are recorded and
131	        reported through notes() rather than raised.
132	        """
133	        plugins: list[Plugin] = []
134	        for name in self.repositories:
135	            try:
136	                plugins.extend(self._load(name))
137	            except Exception as e:
138	                logger.debug("skipping plugin repository %s: %s", name, e)
139	        return plugins
140	
141	    def repo_of(self, plugin: Plugin) -> str | None:
142	        """Which loaded repository served this plugin."""
143	        return self._owner.get(id(plugin))

1	# IDA Plugin Manager
2	
3	The IDA Plugin Manager can help you discover, install, and manage IDA plugins distributed via a central index. It simplifies extending IDA capabilities, whether the plugins are written in IDAPython or compiled languages like C/C++.
4	
5	The underlying index of plugins is published at [github.com/HexRaysSA/plugin-repository](https://github.com/HexRaysSA/plugin-repository),
6	 and Hex-Rays maintains [plugins.hex-rays.com](https://plugins.hex-rays.com) as a website showing the available plugins.
7	
8	!!! note "Development status"
9	
10	      The plugin manager is complete, and we’re now in the process of packaging plugins. Documentation updates are ongoing, and minor adjustments are expected.
11	
12	## Quickstart
13	
14	```console
15	❯ hcli plugin search

37

40	
41	Legacy plugins are old, single-file plugins.
42	They aren't managed by HCLI. Try finding an updated version in the plugin repository.
43	```
44	
45	!!! note "Coming Soon"
46	
47	      We plan to provide an IDA-native GUI for listing, installing, upgrading, and removing plugins in a future release.
48	
49	
50	
51	## Python environment
52	
53	Plugins that declare Python dependencies need a working Python environment. HCLI checks this before installing dependencies. If something is wrong, the install stops and points you to `hcli ida python doctor` for details. See [IDA's Python Environment](ida-python-environment.md) for setup.
54	
55	If your Python setup works but does not match the recommended configuration, pass `--no-python-environment-check` to skip the check:
56	
57	```console
58	❯ hcli plugin --no-python-environment-check install <name>
59	```
60	
61	## As a user of IDA...
62	
63	You'll want to know the HCLI commands:
64	
65	```
66	❯ hcli plugin search 
67	❯ hcli plugin search [keyword or plugin-name]
68	❯ hcli plugin install <plugin-name>
69	❯ hcli plugin status
70	❯ hcli plugin upgrade <plugin-name>
71	❯ hcli plugin uninstall <plugin-name>
72	```
73	
74	Plugins are written to `$IDAUSR/plugins`, which is typically `~/.idapro/plugins` on Unix-like systems, where IDA Pro will load them the next time the application is opened.
75	
76	You can discover interesting plugins via:
77	
78	  - `hcli plugin search` CLI program, or
79	  - [plugins.hex-rays.com](https://plugins.hex-rays.com) website, or
80	  - [github.com/HexRaysSA/plugin-repository](https://github.com/HexRaysSA/plugin-repository) raw index data.
81	
82	HCLI supports installing plugins to be loaded by IDA 9.0 and newer.
83	
84	### Plugin repositories
85	
86	HCLI ships with two built-in repositories (`hexrays` and `community`) that provide the public plugin index. You can add your own named repositories that point to a JSON index file, a local directory of plugin archives, or a [plugin bundle](../reference/plugin-bundle-spec.md) zip.
87	
88	```
89	❯ hcli plugin repo list
90	❯ hcli plugin repo add <name> <url>
91	❯ hcli plugin repo remove <name>
92	❯ hcli plugin repo set-default <name>
93	```
94	
95	Repository URLs use the `https://` scheme for remote JSON indexes or `file://` for local paths. HCLI infers the repository type from what the path points to: a directory becomes a filesystem repository, a zip file containing `plugin-bundle.json` becomes a bundle repository, and anything else is treated as a JSON index.
96	
97	You can scope plugin references to a specific repository with a `repo/` prefix (e.g., `hcli plugin install myrepo/plugin-name`). Unprefixed references resolve against the default repository.
98	
99	### Offline and air-gapped environments
100	
101	Environments without internet access (for example, a FLARE-VM instance with host-only networking) can use a plugin bundle as their sole repository. A plugin bundle is a self-contained zip archive with plugins and their Python dependencies for specific platforms. See [Plugin Bundles](../reference/plugin-bundle-spec.md) for the format.
102	
103	To set this up, remove the default repositories (which require network access), add the bundle as a named repository, and set it as the default:
104	
105	```console
106	❯ hcli plugin repo remove hexrays
107	removed plugin repository 'hexrays'
108	
109	❯ hcli plugin repo remove community
110	removed plugin repository 'community'
111	
112	❯ hcli plugin repo add offline file:///path/to/plugin-bundle.zip
113	added plugin repository 'offline' -> file:///path/to/plugin-bundle.zip
114	
115	❯ hcli plugin repo set-default offline
116	default plugin repository is now 'offline'
117	
118	❯ hcli plugin search
119	current platform: windows-x86_64
120	current version: 9.4
121	
122	 plugin1  1.0.0  ...
123	
124	❯ hcli plugin install plugin1
125	Installed plugin: plugin1==1.0.0
126	```
127	
128	Dependencies are installed from the bundle's embedded wheelhouse, so pip does not need network access.
129	
130	To restore the default configuration later, re-add the built-in repositories with their canonical URLs:
131	
132	```console
133	❯ hcli plugin repo add hexrays https://hexrays.plugins.hex-rays.com/plugin-repository.json
134	❯ hcli plugin repo add community https://community.plugins.hex-rays.com/plugin-repository.json
135	```
136	
137	### Disambiguating plugin names
138	
139	When two plugins share the same bare name in the repository (for example, different forks of the same project), HCLI cannot tell which one you mean from the name alone. The `search`, `install`, and `upgrade` commands will print the ambiguous candidates and ask you to qualify the reference with the plugin's repository URL:
140	
141	```console
142	❯ hcli plugin install ida-chat
143	Error: plugin name 'ida-chat' is ambiguous
144	Choose one of:
145	  ida-chat@https://github.com/HexRaysSA/ida-chat-plugin
146	  ida-chat@https://github.com/tanu360/ida-chat-plugin
147	```
148	
149	You can pin the reference with `name@repository-url`, and optionally include a version spec:
150	
151	```console
152	❯ hcli plugin install ida-chat@https://github.com/HexRaysSA/ida-chat-plugin
153	❯ hcli plugin install ida-chat==1.0.0@https://github.com/HexRaysSA/ida-chat-plugin
154	```
155	
156	Because plugins install into `$IDAUSR/plugins/<name>`, only one plugin with a given bare name can be installed at a time. If you need to switch to a different same-named plugin from another repository, uninstall the current one first. Similarly, `upgrade` will not change the source repository: once a plugin is installed, its repository is recorded in the local metadata and upgrades are anchored to it.
157	
158	
159	## As a plugin author...
160	
161	Hex-Rays wants to help you package and distribute plugins for IDA!
162	Check out the following resources and don't hesitate to contact us for support:
163	
164	  - [Plugin repository architecture](../reference/plugin-repository-architecture.md)
165	  - [Plugin packaging and format](../reference/plugin-packaging-and-format.md)
166	  - [Publishing your existing plugin](../reference/packaging-your-existing-plugin.md)
167	  - [Plugin bundles](../reference/plugin-bundle-spec.md) for offline distribution

Now addressing the user's request to merge `self.repositories` and `self._repos` in aggregate.py. Let me look at how they're used.

`self.repositories` is `dict[str, PluginRepository]` (config-level: name, url, reserved flag). `self._repos` is `dict[str, BasePluginRepo]` (loaded repo objects). They're fundamentally different types -- one is configuration, the other is a loaded instance. They can't be merged cleanly because `self.repositories` is passed in at construction time (before any loading happens) and is iterated to know which repos exist, while `self._repos` is populated lazily during `_load`.

However, looking at the usage pattern: `self.repositories` is only used for:
1. Checking if a name exists (`name not in self.repositories`)
2. Getting the config URL (`self.repositories[name].url`)
3. Iterating all names (`for name in self.repositories`)

We could store `self.repositories` as a dict mapping name to a richer object, but the types are different. Let me look more carefully at how to simplify.

Looking at this carefully: `self.repositories` (`dict[str, PluginRepository]`) and `self._repos` (`dict[str, BasePluginRepo]`) store different things. `PluginRepository` is a config-level dataclass (name, url, reserved), while `BasePluginRepo` is the loaded repo object. They can't be type-merged.

But I can see the user's point -- there's overlap. The callers that access `self.repositories` externally only need:
1. To check if a name is configured: `name not in aggregate.repositories`  
2. To get the URL for error messages: `aggregate.repositories[name].url`

We can keep `self.repositories` as the source-of-truth for "what names are configured" and the loaded `_repos` as an internal cache. The cleanest approach is to keep both but not expose `_repos` -- callers already use `get_child_repo()` to get the loaded object. This is the current design.

Actually, looking at the external callers of `self.repositories`:
- `__init__.py:200`: `name not in aggregate.repositories`
- `__init__.py:216`: `aggregate.repositories[name].url`

These need the config-level info (existence check, URL). The loaded child repos don't have this info. So the two dicts serve different roles and merging them would lose the config metadata or require a wrapper type.

I think the current separation is correct. But let me see if the user wants something simpler -- maybe just renaming `self.repositories` to `self._configs` and making `_repos` the public `repositories` dict? That would be confusing because `repositories` populates lazily. Let me explain to the user.

Actually wait -- I can look at this differently. The user's suggestion was "use the dict form as self.repositories". What if we change `self.repositories` to store a richer object that combines config + loaded repo? Like a dict of `{name: PluginRepository | loaded_repo}`? No, that's messy.

The simplest improvement: since `_repos` is only ever accessed through `get_child_repo()`, and the only external attribute access on `self.repositories` is for `.url` in error messages and membership tests, these really are serving different purposes. I'll keep them separate but let me check if there are other callers.

It calls `find_current_python_executable()` which tries to probe via idat. The simplest fix: the CLI integration tests that exercise the bundle install path need `HCLI_CURRENT_IDA_PYTHON_EXE` set. I can use the `virtual_ida_environment_with_venv` fixture, or more minimally, just set the env var to the current Python interpreter since the test doesn't actually install Python dependencies (the plugin in the test is a simple archive).

Let me check: does the install path actually try to use pip? Looking at the install code, when the repo is a `PluginBundleRepo`, it calls `detect_current_python_version()` to find the wheelhouse target. Then it calls `bundle_dependency_source` which extracts the wheelhouse. If the plugin has no Python dependencies, `install_plugin_archive` just writes the plugin files without pip.

The simplest fix: set `HCLI_CURRENT_IDA_PYTHON_EXE` to the test interpreter in the bundle test. Let me check whether the filesystem repo test also has this issue:

The fs repo test (`test_airgapped_workflow_fs_repo`) only does install, not upgrade. And when installing from a `FileSystemPluginRepo`, the install code checks `isinstance(plugin_repo_obj, PluginBundleRepo)` which is False for fs repos, so it skips the bundle path. So only the bundle test fails.

def test_block_network_blocks_subprocess_http(block_network):
    """The block_network fixture must prevent subprocess HTTP requests (urllib)."""
    import subprocess
    import sys

    try:
        result = subprocess.run(
            [sys.executable, "-c", "import urllib.request; urllib.request.urlopen('http://example.com', timeout=5)"],
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            timeout=10,
            check=False,
        )
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        # On Windows the dead proxy can cause a hang rather than a fast refusal;
        # a timeout still proves the network path is blocked.
        return
    assert result.returncode != 0
    assert "ProxyError" in result.stderr or "URLError" in result.stderr or "ConnectionRefusedError" in result.stderr
